title.zh: 卷六 帝紀第六 中宗元帝 肅宗明帝
title.en: Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Yuan; Emperor Ming
title.raw: 卷六 帝紀第六 中宗元帝 肅宗明帝 Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Yuan; Emperor Ming

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 元皇帝諱睿，字景文，宣帝曾孫，琅邪恭王覲之子也。
value.en: Emperor Yuan, whose personal name was Rui and courtesy name Jingwen, was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of Jin and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.
value.literal: The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.

value.zh: 咸寧二年生於洛陽，有神光之異，一室盡明，所藉槁如始刈。
value.en: He was born in Luoyang in 276, amid a strange glow that lit the whole chamber and left the bedding straw looking freshly mown.
value.literal: In the second year of Xianning he was born in Luoyang; there was a divine radiance anomaly; one room was entirely bright; the straw on which he lay was as if newly cut.

value.zh: 及長，白豪生於日角之左，隆準龍顏，目有精曜，顧眄煒如也。
value.en: As a man he bore a white filament beside the auspicious bump on his forehead, the high-bridged "dragon" profile of a ruler, and eyes so bright that every turn of his gaze seemed to flash with light.
value.literal: When grown, a white hair grew to the left of his sun-corner; high bridge nose and dragon countenance; his eyes had refined brilliance; his glances were radiant.

value.zh: 年十五，嗣位琅邪王。
value.en: At fifteen he inherited the title of Prince of Langye.
value.literal: At age fifteen he succeeded to the position of Prince of Langye.

value.zh: 幼有令問。
value.en: Even as a boy he was already known for an excellent name.
value.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation.

value.zh: 及惠皇之際，王室多故，帝每恭儉退讓，以免於禍。
value.en: Under Emperor Hui, when the house of Jin was rocked by one crisis after another, he habitually kept to modesty, frugality, and deference so as to stay clear of disaster.
value.literal: When it came to the time of Emperor Hui, the royal house had many troubles; the emperor each time was respectful, frugal, yielding, in order to avoid calamity.

value.zh: 沈敏有度量，不顯灼然之迹，故時人未之識焉。
value.en: He was steady, astute, and large-minded, yet never advertised his abilities, so his contemporaries failed to see the ruler in him.
value.literal: Deep and keen, with capacity for tolerance, he did not display glaring traces; therefore people of the time did not recognize him.

value.zh: 惟侍中嵇紹異之，謂人曰：「琅邪王毛骨非常，殆非人臣之相也。」
value.en: Only Ji Shao, the palace attendant, saw something different in him and told others, "The Prince of Langye has a presence no ordinary man possesses; that is hardly the look of someone born to serve another."
value.literal: Only Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Shao thought him strange, saying to people: "The Prince of Langye's bearing is extraordinary; probably it is not the appearance of a subject."

value.zh: 二月，葬元帝于建平陵，帝徒跣至于陵所。
value.en: In the second month Emperor Yuan was laid in the Jianping tombs; the new emperor walked the last miles barefoot behind the bier.
value.literal: In the second month they buried Yuan Emperor at Jianping Mausoleum; the emperor barefoot went to the mausoleum site.

value.zh: 以特進華恒爲驃騎將軍、都督石頭水陸軍事。
value.en: Hua Heng, holding the title specially advanced, was named general of agile cavalry and commander of land and river forces at Stone City.
value.literal: He appointed Specially Advanced Hua Heng as General of Agile Cavalry, Area Commander-in-Chief of Stone Rampart water and land military affairs.

value.zh: 乙丑，黃霧四塞。
value.en: On the yichou day yellow fog closed in on every side.
value.literal: On yichou yellow fog filled the four directions.

value.zh: 丙寅，隕霜。
value.en: Frost fell on the bingyin day.
value.literal: On bingyin frost fell.

value.zh: 壬申，又隕霜，殺穀。
value.en: On renshen frost struck again and blighted the crops.
value.literal: On renshen again frost fell, killing grain.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 元后既崩，悼后繼作，至楊駿肆逆，禍延天母。
value.en: After Yang Yan died came Yang Zhi; Yang Jun’s treason dragged down the queen mother.
value.literal: After the primal empress died, the mourned empress succeeded; when Yang Jun ran riot, calamity reached the Mother of Heaven.

value.zh: 孝懷皇帝追復號諡，豈不以鯀殛禹興，義在不替者乎！
value.en: Huai restored her honors—as Gun fell but Yu rose, duty survives.
value.literal: Emperor Huai restored her title and epithet—is this not because Gun was executed yet Yu rose—the principle of unbroken obligation?

value.zh: 又太寧二年，臣忝宗正，帝譜泯棄，罔所循按。
value.en: In Taining 316 I held the clan office; registers were gone.
value.literal: Moreover in the second Taining year I humbly served as Director of the Imperial Clan; imperial genealogies were lost—nothing to consult.

value.zh: 時博諮舊齒，以定昭穆，與故驃騎將軍華恒、尚書荀崧、侍中荀邃因舊譜參論撰次，尊號之重，一無改替。
value.en: With Hua Heng, Xun Song, and Xun Sui we recomposed charts—her rank stood firm.
value.literal: We broadly queried elders to fix generations and, with former General of Agile Cavalry Hua Heng, Minister Xun Song, Palace Attendant Xun Sui, reviewed old lists to compile order—her lofty title stayed unchanged.

value.zh: 今聖上孝思，祗肅禋祀，詢及群司，將以恢定大禮。
value.en: Today’s ruler seeks your counsel to fix court ritual.
value.literal: Now our sage sovereign’s filial care solemnly tends sacrifice; he asks all bureaus to settle great ritual.

value.zh: 臣輒思詳，伏見惠皇帝起居注、群臣議奏，列駿作逆謀，危社稷，引魯之文姜，漢之呂后。
value.en: Hui’s archives cite Wen Jiang and Empress Lü against Yang Jun.
value.literal: I have reflected carefully: in Emperor Hui’s daily records and ministers’ memorials they listed Jun’s treason, imperiling altars, citing Lu’s Wen Jiang and Han’s Empress Lü.

value.zh: 臣竊以文姜雖莊公之母，實為父讎；
value.en: Wen Jiang was Duke Huan’s killer despite bearing Zhuang—
value.literal: I quietly note that although Wen Jiang was Duke Zhuang’s mother, she was truly her husband’s foe;

value.zh: 呂后寵樹私戚，幾危劉氏，按此二事異于今日。
value.en: Empress Lü nearly ruined Han—these differ from Yang Zhi.
value.literal: Empress Lü favored kin until she nearly ended the Liu house—these two cases differ from today.

value.zh: 昔漢章帝竇后殺和帝之母，和帝即位盡誅諸竇。
value.en: Zhangdi’s Dou killed He’s mother; He wiped out the Dous.
value.literal: Formerly Dou empress of Han Zhangdi killed Emperor He’s mother; when He ascended he slaughtered the Dou clan.

value.zh: 當時議者欲貶竇后，及后之亡，欲不以禮葬。
value.en: Critics then sought to shame Dou and withhold burial rites.
value.literal: Debates then wished to demote Dou empress; when she died some wished denial of ritual burial.

value.zh: 和帝以奉事十年，義不可違，臣子之道，務從豐厚，仁明之稱，表于往代。
value.en: He refused cruelty after ten years’ care—his mercy became legend.
value.literal: He had served her ten years—duty forbade cruelty; ministers pursued lavish burial—his humanity shone for ages.

value.zh: 又見故尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事，稱繼母雖出，追服無改。
value.en: Pei Yi argued Emperor Ai’s mourned empress kept mourning even after divorce.
value.literal: I also saw former Minister Director Pei Yi’s opinion on Empress Dao’s case—though a stepmother had departed, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.

value.zh: 是以孝懷皇帝尊崇號諡，還葬峻陵。
value.en: So Huai restored her posthumous honors at Junling.
value.literal: Therefore Emperor Huai restored honored title and epithet and reburied her at Jun Mausoleum.

value.zh: 此則母子道全，而廢事蕩革也。
value.en: Kin duty survived though politics had fouled them.
value.literal: Thus mother-son duty stayed whole while violent deeds were swept away.

value.zh: 于時祭于弘訓之宮，未入太廟。
value.en: She received offerings only at Hongxun, not the grand temple.
value.literal: At that time sacrifice occurred at Hongxun Palace—not yet entering the great temple.

value.zh: 蓋是事之未盡，非義典也。
value.en: That showed work unfinished, not proper liturgy.
value.literal: That was because the matter was unfinished—not canonical meaning.

value.zh: 若以悼后復位為宜，則應配食世祖；
value.en: If Yang Zhi deserves restoration, she must join Wu’s temple;
value.literal: If restoring Empress Dao is right, she should share Emperor Wu’s offerings;

value.zh: 若以復之為非，則譜諡宜闕，未有位號居正，而偏祠別室者也。
value.en: if not, her titles should lapse—no legitimate rank receives only a side altar.
value.literal: if restoring her is wrong, then genealogies and epithets should lapse—one cannot hold orthodox rank yet dwell in a side shrine alone.

value.zh: 若以孝懷皇帝私隆母子之道，特為立廟者，此苟崇私情，有虧國典，則國譜帝諱，皆宜除棄，匪徒不得同祀于世祖之廟也。
value.en: A private shrine for filial piety alone would break precedent and void every register.
value.literal: If Emperor Huai privately enlarged mother-son feeling and built a special temple, that would exalt private affection yet wound state canon—then clan registers and temple names should all be discarded, not merely barred from Wu’s temple.

value.zh: 永嘉元年，追復尊號，別立廟，神主不配武帝。
value.en: In 307 her title was restored, a separate shrine was built, and her tablet was not enshrined with Emperor Wu.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongjia her honored title was restored, a separate temple was established, and her spirit tablet was not paired with Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 至成帝咸康七年，下詔使內外詳議。
value.en: In 341 Emperor Cheng ordered court and capital officials to deliberate the question fully.
value.literal: By the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered inner and outer officials to debate the matter in detail.

value.zh: 衛將軍虞潭議曰：世祖武皇帝光有四海，元皇后應乾作配。
value.en: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Emperor Wu illumined the realm; his first empress answered Heaven.”
value.literal: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Shizu Emperor Wu glorified the four seas; his primal empress matched Heaven’s pivot.”

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第094卷
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 94
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 94

value.zh: 乙未，峻逼遷帝於石頭。
value.en: On day Yiwei, Su Jun forced the emperor to move to Stone City.
value.literal: On day Yiwei, Jun compelled the relocation of the emperor to Stone City.

value.zh: 司徒導固爭，不從。
value.en: Grand Tutor Wang Dao protested fiercely but was overruled.
value.literal: Grand Tutor Dao remonstrated firmly but was not heeded.

value.zh: 帝哀泣升車，宮中慟哭。
value.en: The emperor wept as he boarded the carriage; the palace echoed with mourning.
value.literal: The emperor wept in grief as he mounted the carriage; within the palace there was wailing.

value.zh: 時天大雨，道路泥濘，劉超、鐘雅步侍左右。
value.en: It rained heavily; the roads were mud; Liu Chao and Zhong Ya walked at his side through it all.
value.literal: At the time Heaven sent great rain; the roads were mire; Liu Chao and Zhong Ya walked in attendance at left and right.

value.zh: 峻給馬，不肯乘，而悲哀慷慨。
value.en: Su Jun offered horses; they refused to ride, grieving yet defiant.
value.literal: Jun provided horses; they refused to mount, yet were mournful and resolute.

value.zh: 峻聞而惡之，然未敢殺也。
value.en: Su Jun hated this but dared not kill them.
value.literal: Jun heard and hated this, yet did not dare kill them.

value.zh: 以其親信許方等補司馬督、殿中監，外托宿衛，內實防禦超等。
value.en: He made his confidant Xu Fang Commander of the Army and Palace Director—nominally for palace guard, in truth to watch Liu Chao and the others.
value.literal: He appointed his trusted follower Xu Fang and others as Commander of the Army and Palace Director—outwardly entrusted with night guard, inwardly really to guard against Chao and the rest.

value.zh: 峻以倉屋為帝宮，日來帝前肆丑言。
value.en: Su Jun housed the emperor in granary buildings and came each day to hurl insults at him.
value.literal: Jun made granary buildings the emperor's palace and daily came before the emperor to vent foul speech.

value.zh: 劉超、鐘雅與右光祿大夫荀崧、金紫光祿大夫華恆、尚書荀邃、侍中丁潭侍從，不離帝側。
value.en: Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Right Grand Master of the Bright Xu Song, Grand Master of the Golden Purple Hua Heng, Secretary Xun Sui, and Palace Attendant Ding Tan never left the emperor's side.
value.literal: Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Right Grand Master of the Bright Xu Song, Grand Master of the Golden Purple Hua Heng, Secretary Xun Sui, and Palace Attendant Ding Tan attended in service and did not leave the emperor's side.

value.zh: 時饑饉，米貴，峻問遺，超一無所受，繾綣朝夕，臣節愈恭；
value.en: Famine had driven rice prices high; when Su Jun sent gifts, Liu Chao refused every one; day and night he tended the emperor, his loyalty growing ever more reverent;
value.literal: At the time there was famine; rice was costly; Jun sent gifts; Chao accepted none; day and night he was devoted; his ministerial conduct grew ever more respectful;

value.zh: 雖居幽厄之中，超猶啟帝，授《孝經》、《論語》。
value.en: though held captive, Liu Chao still taught the emperor the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
value.literal: though dwelling in dire straits, Chao still instructed the emperor, teaching him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

value.zh: 右衛將軍齊超、侍中鐘雅與建康令管旆等謀奉帝出赴西軍；
value.en: Right Guard General Qi Chao, Palace Attendant Zhong Ya, and Jiankang Prefect Guan Pei and others plotted to take the emperor out to the western armies;
value.literal: Right Guard General Qi Chao, Palace Attendant Zhong Ya, and Jiankang Prefect Guan Pei and others plotted to escort the emperor out to join the western armies;

value.zh: 事洩，蘇逸使其將平原任讓將兵入宮收超、雅。
value.en: when the plot leaked, Su Yi sent his general Ren Rang of Pingyuan with troops into the palace to seize Chao and Ya.
value.literal: The plot leaked; Su Yi sent his general Pingyuan Ren Rang with troops into the palace to seize Chao and Ya.

value.zh: 帝抱持悲泣曰：「還我侍中、右衛！」
value.en: The emperor clung to them, weeping: "Give me back my palace attendant and my right guard!"
value.literal: The emperor clung to them weeping: "Give me back my palace attendant and right guard!"

value.zh: 讓奪而殺之。
value.en: Ren Rang tore them from his arms and killed them.
value.literal: Rang snatched them away and killed them.

value.zh: 初，讓少無行，太常華恆為本州大中正，黜其品。
value.en: Ren Rang had been dissolute in his youth. Hua Heng, Grand Master of Ceremonies and chief provincial arbiter of ranks, had lowered his standing.
value.literal: Earlier, Rang in youth had no proper conduct; Grand Master of Ceremonies Hua Heng as provincial chief arbiter of ranks demoted his grade.

value.zh: 及讓為蘇峻將，乘勢多所誅殺，見恆輒恭敬，不敢縱暴。
value.en: After he became one of Su Jun's generals and rode the tide of power, he killed many—but whenever he saw Hua Heng he behaved with deference and did not dare abuse his authority.
value.literal: When Rang became Su Jun's general, riding the momentum he killed many; when he saw Heng he always showed respect and did not dare act violently.

value.zh: 及鐘、劉之死，蘇逸欲並殺恆，讓盡心救衛，恆乃得免。
value.en: When Zhong Ya and Liu Chao died, Su Yi wanted to kill Hua Heng as well. Ren Rang threw himself into protecting him, and Heng was spared.
value.literal: At the deaths of Zhong and Liu, Su Yi wished to kill Heng as well; Rang exerted himself to save and protect him, and Heng thus escaped.
